title: Tritium safety licensing frameworks
bottleneck: No regulator has yet licensed a commercial fusion power plant, and tritium, mobile, radioactive, and biologically active as tritiated water, sits at the center of the safety case. Source-term definitions, allowable release limits, and accident scenarios for kilogram-scale tritium inventories are still being negotiated between developers and regulators. Overly conservative rules could make plants uneconomic; lax ones risk public acceptance.
why_it_blocks: Fusion's social license depends on credible tritium safety. A single significant release incident at an early plant could set the industry back a decade regardless of the technology's merits.
current_state: The US NRC and UK regulators are developing fusion-specific frameworks distinct from fission rules. No commercial fusion plant has completed licensing anywhere. Developers are engaging regulators early through pre-application processes, but binding safety criteria for tritium handling remain undefined.
